channel.title: English Radio
channel.description: A British English radio show for the commute: farming and technology, everyday chat, and IELTS words in context.
channel.itunes:author: English Radio

item.title: 1. Smart Collars for Dairy Cows
item.description: A vet from New Zealand explains how sensors on cows spot illness and heat early. Then Sonia and Ryan talk about the daily commute.

item.title: 2. Milk and Mobile Money in Kenya
item.description: How small dairy farms in Kenya feed their cows, sell their milk and get paid by phone. Then a report on plant-based milk, and a chat about tea.

item.title: 3. Drones on the Farm
item.description: An Australian agronomist on mapping and spraying crops with drones. Then a report on the four-day working week, and a chat about winter weather.

item.title: 4. From Milk to Cheese
item.description: An Irish cheesemaker explains how milk becomes cheese. Then a report on the global rise of Japanese city pop, and a chat about breakfast.

item.title: 5. The Sound of Africa
item.description: A music journalist from Lagos explains how Afrobeats went global. Then a report on the vinyl revival, and a chat about the British pub.

item.title: 6. The Life Under Our Feet
item.description: A Canadian soil scientist on what soil really is, how farmers protect it, and how to measure soil moisture. Then a report on British allotments, and a chat about Christmas.

item.title: 7. Swahili and the Spice Island
item.description: A teacher from Zanzibar talks about the Swahili language, greetings, food and the history of the Spice Island. Then a report on words English borrowed from other languages, and a chat about street food.

item.title: 8. Farms in the Sky
item.description: An urban farmer from Singapore explains rooftop farms, vertical farms and food security in a small city. Then a report on the global matcha boom, and a chat about karaoke.

item.title: 9. Food and Faith
item.description: A food writer from Mumbai explains how religion shapes what people eat in India and around the world. Then a report on Britain's love of curry, and a chat about listening to music while you work.

item.title: 10. Maize, Rain and Resilience
item.description: A South African agronomist on maize, drought and small farms in Malawi and Zambia. Then a report on Glastonbury, the music festival on a dairy farm, and Sonia and Ryan look back on ten episodes.

item.title: 11. Late Night Special: The Queue That Wasn't
item.description: A comedy special. Embarrassing stories, brutal nicknames, silly listener mail, and a crash course in British sarcasm.
